newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Demand rises on Bulgaria depo market ahead of peg.
newsitem.headline: Demand rises on Bulgaria depo market ahead of peg.

text.p: Demand for interbank deposits rose sharply on the Bulgarian money market as banks sought levs for pending payments and foreign currency buying ahead of a currency board peg, dealers said.
"Banks bid for large amounts of funds for tax and salary payments due by end-month and to pay for government securities they bought at auctions on Monday and Tuesday," a commercial bank dealer said.

Demand for levs rose also due to foreign currency buying as potential profit from it was seen higher than yields on government securities in the period to July 1 when the lev is to be pegged at 1,000 per mark under a currency board system.
The lev traded near 990 against the mark and around 1,700 to the dollar at 1225 GMT on the local interbank forex market.

The average yield to maturity on four-week discount T-bills, auctioned daily by the Finance Ministry, fell to 0.40 percent on Wednesday from 0.42 at Tuesday's auction, 0.47 percent on Monday and 0.58 on Friday.
Banks had to pay on Wednesday for four T-bill issues with a total par of 75 billion levs they bought in the past two days.
"On Tuesday and Wednesday some banks offered for sale the T-bills they bought on Monday to raise lev funds to pay for the paper at today's settlement," another dealer said.
Overnight interbank depo rates stood at 11-12 percent annually, unchanged from Tuesday. The simple annual rates for lending for up to seven days stood at 15-16 percent, also flat.
The average annual interbank deposit rate was 14.82 percent on Tuesday against 12.27 percent on Monday, a central bank official said.

The simple monthly main interest rate was 1.27 percent under the central bank effective annual main interest rate of 16.30 percent that took effect from Monday, central bank figures showed. -- Dessislava Popova, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
